items.title: Avakian George — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: In my freshman year – as a matter of fact, this began in my senior year at Horace Mann – Les Koenig told me about the book that Hughes Panassié had written in French. He had a copy, which he had imported somehow. I don’t recall how I got Panassié’s address. It was of course not in the book itself. B

ctx.x: It was the one tune that I knew. I didn’t know much about the others. So Les played me more Armstrong and played me some of the Hot Fives and Sevens, which I found awful primitive sounding. I wasn’t used to listening to an acoustic recording. I didn’t like them all that much, but it did open my ears to the fact that there were people I had brushed off as being kind of shallow, maybe. Imagine thinking Armstrong was a shallow performer when you first heard him, but that was because I didn’t know better and I didn’t…
